checkpoint_review: I agree with the Router's assessment on all visible checkpoints. The head features (comb, wattle, beak, eye) are clearly rendered and correct. The plumage characteristics (hackle, saddle, iridescence) are present and match the 'cock' class definition. Regarding the limbs: The Router correctly identified that the spur and toe count are not testable due to occlusion by the perch and image resolution. While the legs are visible, the specific diagnostic details required for a positive check are genuinely obscured, making 'is_present: false' (or effectively untestable) the correct conservative verdict. No checkpoints were marked as present when they should have been missing.
artifact_review: The Router identified texture anomalies in the hackles and structural collapse at the neck-body junction. I agree these are present but believe the severity is slightly underestimated. The neck-to-body transition exhibits significant 'mushing' where red and black feathers blend without distinct layering, resembling a paint smear rather than overlapping keratin. Additionally, upon closer inspection of the tail, there is a subtle artifact: the sickle feathers appear to fuse into a single solid mass near the base before separating, lacking the individual strand definition expected in high-quality imagery. The leg scaling also appears somewhat smooth/plastic-like rather than distinctly reptilian. These cumulative textural issues warrant a lower artifact score than the formula suggests.
alignment_reasoning: 9/11 checkpoints passed. The two failed checkpoints (spur, toes) are legitimately occluded/untestable rather than missing anatomy. Expert visual confirmation supports strong alignment with the target class 'cock'.
artifact_reasoning: Router correctly flagged neck texture and fusion. Severity adjusted upward due to additional observation of tail feather fusion at the base and plastic-like leg texture. The 'painted' look of the hackles and muddy transition zone are notable generation artifacts.
key_defects: Muddy/fused transition between red hackles and black body feathers
Overly smooth, airbrushed texture on neck plumage lacking strand definition
Tail sickle feathers fusing into a solid mass at the base
